messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Error with saalfeld xform
parts:
Dear Ansh, thanks for your interest in nat and sorry you’ve run into trouble here. Could you run 

nat.h5reg::dr_h5reg()

and report what it says? For good measure you could also run 

sessioninfo::session_info()

All the best,

Greg.

On 1 Feb 2021, at 19:55, Ansh Gandhi <haduke...@gmail.com> wrote:

﻿Hey all,

I am trying to transform a neuron that I have retrieved from hemibrain to FAFB space, then plot it 3-dimensionally using this code:
library(natverse); library(nat.jrcbrains);
LHAV1a1.hemibrain = neuprint_read_neurons("LHAV1a1");
LHAV1a1.hemibrain.fafb = xform_brain(LHAV1a1.hemibrain*8/1000, reference= "FAFB14", sample="JRCFIB2018F", via=JRC2018F);
plot3d(LHAV1a1.hemibrain.fafb, lwd=2); plot3d(FAFB);

However, when running, the code never gets past the xform_brain command and throws this error consistently:
Transforming neurons using the sequence: JRCFIB2018F->JRC2018F->FAFB14um->FAFB14
Error in saalfeld_xform(points, reg, inverse = !swapped, ...) : 
  Error running saalfeld xform!

As a result, only the FAFB space is plotted without the transformed neuron. I am relatively new to this, so this may be a simple fix, but I can't seem to figure it out.

Any and all help would be very much appreciated!

Sincerely,
Ansh Gandhi

parts:
Hi Dr. Jefferis,

 

Thanks for the prompt reply! I actually managed to solve the error by running that first command. It threw a few errors, and I realized that my computer did not have a JDK set up on it due to the fact that it is relatively new. I set up the latest Oracle JDK and set my PATH variables, and the registration worked like it was supposed to! This is why I deleted the post.

 

Thank you for the help!

 

Sincerely,

Ansh Gandhi
